extracted.intended_audience: applicants, owners, agents, IP office staff, and legal practitioners dealing with industrial design and trade name registration and enforcement in Member States
extracted.subtask_short: industrial design and trade name registration
extracted.subtask_description: Official rules and substantive/procedural criteria for filing, examination, opposition, registration, enforcement, renewals, restoration, transfer, licensing and penalties relating to industrial designs and trade names under the Agreement/Annex. Covers required contents, time limits, grounds for rejection/invalidity and remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection only if opposition well-founded
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization may only reject the application for registration if the opposition is well-founded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rejection ruling shall be published in the Official Bulletin of the Organization; the Organization’s ruling on the opposition is appealable to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days from notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership — timing and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: An entitled person may claim ownership of an application before the Organization within three months of the publication of the application by submitting a written notice setting forth the grounds of his claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization sends a copy of the notice to the applicant/agent who may submit a reasoned reply within three months, renewable once on request; parties may be heard before ruling; transfer only if claim is well-founded; final decision published in special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications — when permitted and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: An initial application concerning several designs may be divided into divisional applications: (a) at least until decision on registration; (b) during opposition or claim-of-ownership proceedings; and (c) during appellate proceedings concerning opposition or claim of ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divisional applications retain the filing date of the initial application and, if applicable, the benefit of the priority date; a fee is required for each divisional application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of application — formal conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall examine all applications to determine whether the formal conditions referred to in Articles 8 and 9 of the Annex have been met and the requisite fees paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conditions met, the Organization shall register and publish the industrial design; the legal date of registration is the filing date; Organization may correct obvious clerical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defect notification and remedy period
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application failing to fulfill the prescribed conditions (Article 8 except sub‑paragraph 1(b), and Article 9) shall be considered defective and the defect notified to the applicant or agent, who is invited to remedy it within three months of notification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This time limit may be extended for 30 days on request where a justifiable need exists; the remedied application retains the date of the initial application; if rectified documents are not provided within time limit, application is rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: No rejection without opportunity to correct
rubrics_metrics.description: No filing may be rejected under specified paragraphs without affording the applicant or his agent the opportunity to rectify it to the extent and according to the prescribed forms and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection shall be issued by the Director-General and the applicant may appeal to the High Commission of Appeal within 60 days of notification; final rejection published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of certificate — required contents (industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once registration is completed, the owner shall be issued a certificate containing: registration number; filing number of the application; filing date; class under the Locarno Classification; products to which the design applies; company name or owner name and address; and validly claimed priority, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Organization shall attach graphical or photographical representations of the industrial design to the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of registration — required information (industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Organization shall publish for each certificate: registration number; filing number; filing date; Locarno class; title of the design; company name or owner name and address; creator name and address (unless requested omitted); validly claimed priority; priority date/country/earlier application number; agent name/address (if applicable); and registration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing regulations determine procedures for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection and renewals (industrial design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection expires at the end of the fifth year from the filing date; registration may be renewed for two consecutive five-year periods on owner request and payment of renewal fee fixed by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Renewal fee must be paid within the twelve months preceding expiration; a six-month grace period allowed after expiration subject to surcharge; failure to pay within prescribed time results in forfeiture of rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication and access to application documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions, drawings and photographs of registered industrial designs shall be kept by the Organization and communicated on request after publication; specimens shall be kept for eight years and may be examined by any interested person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons may obtain official copies of descriptions/drawings/photographs after publication; applies to applicants seeking priority and to documents authorizing such priority; applicants may obtain official copy to avail themselves abroad of priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of lapsed protection — timing and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where protection was not renewed owing to circumstances beyond the owner's control, the owner or entitled persons may apply for restoration within six months of the date circumstances ceased to exist and no later than two years from the date renewal was due, on payment of the renewal fee and a surcharge and submitting grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization examines grounds and either restores or rejects; restoration does not extend the maximum duration; third parties who started exploiting design after expiry may continue; restored designs published; rejection appealable within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of preservation (specimens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where designs have not been claimed by their owners within two years following the expiration of protection, specimens of the filed designs shall be destroyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissibility for non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: No filing shall be admissible if the application is not accompanied by a document proving payment to the Organization of the requisite fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of rights — written evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts involving transfer of ownership, licensing of the right of exploitation, assignment, pledge or cancellation of a pledge in respect of a design shall be evidenced in writing on pain of invalidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration/publication of acts binding on third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts mentioned (transfer, license, pledge, etc.) shall not be binding on third parties unless entered in the special register of designs and published in the Official Bulletin; a copy shall be kept by the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization shall furnish copies, records of entries concerning pledges, or certificates attesting absence of such entries on request.

rubrics_metrics.name: License contract formalities and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may license exploitation by contract; the license duration may not exceed the registration duration; the license contract must be evidenced in writing and signed on pain of invalidity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: License contract must be entered in the special register on payment of fee; license is not enforceable against third parties until such entry and publication; entry may be removed on evidence of expiration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalid clauses in license contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clauses in license contracts that constitute anti-competitive practices or impose restrictions not deriving from the rights conferred by the registration or not necessary for upholding such rights shall be invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The competent domestic court shall ascertain invalid clauses at request of any person.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competent court and nature of civil action
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil action relating to industrial designs shall be brought before civil courts and judged as for summary proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where criminal court is seized for counterfeiting, it shall rule on challenges brought by defendant as to invalidity, expiry, or ownership of the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of criminal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal proceedings may be initiated concurrently by the Public Prosecutor’s Office and the prejudiced party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for invalidity of registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration shall be declared invalid by a court decision where: (a) it is not consistent with Articles 1 and 2; (b) the owner could not enjoy the protection in Article 4; (c) the design infringes rights attaching to a prior industrial design disclosed after the filing/priority date and still protected; (d) it infringes the rights of a third party; or (e) it uses a prior protected distinctive sign without authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds in (b)-(e) may be relied on by public prosecutor or any interested person/professional union; if grounds affect only part of registration, registration may be maintained in modified form provided criteria for protection are fulfilled and identity maintained; final judicial decisions communicated to Organization for register entry and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership before the court — time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an industrial design has already been registered, claim of ownership shall be brought before competent domestic court and be time-bound by three years from the publication of the registration; action against a defendant acting in bad faith is not time-bound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final decision transferring the registration must be notified to the Organization for entry and publication; Organization notifies beneficiaries of licenses recorded in special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevention of infringement — urgent measures and evidentiary standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person empowered to bring action may make an urgent application seeking orders to prevent imminent infringement or continuation of alleged counterfeiting. The court may order urgent measures inter partes or ex parte where delay would cause irreparable harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court may order measures only if evidence reasonably accessible to applicant makes it likely that his rights are being infringed or infringement is imminent; court may require guarantees, prohibit acts, order seizure or custodial transfer, or impose conditions to secure compensation; measures ordered prior to proceedings require applicant to take civil or criminal action within 20 days or measures may be cancelled on defendant's application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure for counterfeiting — judicial order and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Prejudiced party may approach bailiff/public/judicial officer (including customs) assisted by an expert to prepare a detailed inventory with or without seizure following an order by the presiding judge within whose jurisdiction operations are conducted, including at the border.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order made on application with proof of registration attached; judge may require security deposit from applicant (always required of foreigners); a copy of the order must be left with custodians of objects and, if necessary, documentation of security deposit on pain of invalidity and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to institute proceedings after seizure
rubrics_metrics.description: If petitioner fails to institute criminal or civil proceedings within 10 working days of the seizure or inventory or the information provided by customs, such seizure or inventory shall ipso jure be void, without prejudice to claimed damages if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of counterfeiting and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of the rights of the owner set forth in Article 3 shall constitute counterfeiting; counterfeiting may be proven by all means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for knowing infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any knowing infringement of the rights enshrined in this Annex shall be punishable by imprisonment for one to three years and a fine of 5,000,000 to 30,000,000 CFA francs or one of these penalties alone, without prejudice to civil damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Penalties for recidivism
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of recidivism or if defendant previously worked for the prejudiced party, the penalties provided shall be doubled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recidivism occurs where, within the previous five years, an offender has been convicted of one of the offenses provided in this Annex; domestic legislation on mitigating circumstances applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional sanctions — deprivation of electoral rights and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to penalties, convicted persons may be deprived of the right to participate in elections to professional groups for up to 10 years; competent domestic court may order posting/insertion of judgment (whole or excerpts) in designated newspapers at convicted person's expense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border measures on request — detention and proof requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: On written application supported by proof of right, customs may detain goods the applicant claims to be counterfeit; public prosecutor, applicant and importer shall be immediately informed of detention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detention lifted ipso jure within 10 working days if applicant fails to provide proof of interim measures or of application to competent national judge and requisite guarantees; applicant may obtain names/addresses/quantity of sender/importer/recipient notwithstanding professional secrecy rules; owner/importer/recipient may suspend detention on payment of security deposit where decision to suspend free movement is not taken by judicial authority or independent administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs ex officio detention
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs authorities may ex officio decide to retain suspect goods where they have prima facie evidence that goods are counterfeit; they may request the owner to provide information to assist in exercising their powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner, importer and exporter shall be immediately informed of detention; customs may incur liability for unjustified detention unless they acted in good faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of materials to courts
rubrics_metrics.description: Any court seized of a dispute may request the Organization to transmit copies of graphical and photographical representations of a filed or registered industrial design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense rights of registered exclusive licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: Any beneficiary of an exclusive contractual license may, by registered letter, call on the owner to bring necessary legal action seeking civil or criminal penalties for reported violations; if owner refuses or fails within three months, the registered licensee may institute action in his own name without prejudice to the owner's right to intervene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Within the Annex, a trade name shall be the name under which a trade, industrial, craft, agricultural or other business establishment is known and exploited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade name inadmissibility (morality/public policy/misleading)
rubrics_metrics.description: A name or designation shall not be admissible as a trade name if, by reason of its nature or the use to which it may be put, it is contrary to morality or public policy and if it is liable to mislead trade circles or the public as to the nature of the establishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to the trade name — priority of use or registration and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name shall belong to the person having first made use of it or having first registered it; use may only be proved by written or printed matter or documents contemporaneous with the facts they seek to establish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where a registered trade name has been publicly and continuously used on national territory for at least five years without well-founded legal action, ownership may not be challenged on priority grounds unless applicant could not have been unaware of the earlier trade name at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific criminal effect only for registered trade names
rubrics_metrics.description: Only trade names registered in accordance with this Annex may be the subject of the criminal penalties specified in Articles 18(3) and 18(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for using trade names — confusion prohibition and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is illegal to use in a Member State a trade name registered for the same activity if such use is liable to create confusion between establishments; however, registered owner may not prevent third parties from use in good faith of their names, addresses, pseudonyms, geographical names, or exact indications concerning kind/quality/quantity/destination/value/origin/time of production for purposes of mere identification or information, provided such use cannot mislead the public as to source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rights to a trade name are subsequent to a registered trade name, person with similar personal name must take measures (e.g., addition) to distinguish his trade name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing requirements for trade name application
rubrics_metrics.description: Owner of an establishment in a Member State may file for registration; application filed with Organization or Ministry according to procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application file shall contain: (a) application addressed to Director-General with applicant's surname/first name/address/nationality, the trade name sought, and location/type of activity; (b) proof of payment of requisite fees; (c) unstamped private power of attorney if represented by an agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report of filing and transmission to Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A report prepared by the Organization or Ministry shall note each filing specifying date and time; a copy issued to applicant. Within five working days the Ministry shall transmit the application to the Organization attaching report, proof of payment and power of attorney (if appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication contents for trade name application
rubrics_metrics.description: For every trade name application, the Organization shall publish: filing number; filing date; trade name and location of establishment; company name or owner name and address; and activities for which registration is sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to trade name — grounds, timing and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may oppose registration of a trade name within three months of publication by sending a written statement setting out reasons based on infringement of Articles 1, 2 and 5(1), or of a prior right belonging to the opposing party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organization sends copy to applicant who may submit a reasoned reply within three months, renewable once; if reply not received by prescribed time limit, applicant deemed to have withdrawn application and registration cancelled; parties may be heard; Organization's ruling appealable within 60 days; registration cancelled only if opposition valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination/registration of trade names — conditions and rectification
rubrics_metrics.description: For trade name applications, once Organization ascertains the trade name is not inconsistent with Article 2, the filing is proper and fees paid, it shall register and publish the trade name; registration takes effect from filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings failing Article 2 requirements rejected; filings failing formal Article 6 requirements (except sub‑paragraph (b)) are irregular and applicant invited to provide proper documents within three months (extendable 30 days); regularized application retains initial filing date; rectified documents not produced within time limit lead to rejection; Director-General notifies rejection; no rejection under specified paragraphs without opportunity to rectify; Organization may correct obvious clerical errors; applicant may appeal rejection within 60 days (decision of High Commission not appealable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issuance of certificate — required contents (trade name)
rubrics_metrics.description: On completion of registration, the owner shall be furnished with a certificate containing: registration number; filing date and filing number and date of registration; the trade name as registered; location of the commercial establishment and type of activity; surname, first name and address of owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of registered trade name information
rubrics_metrics.description: Organization shall publish the information in Article 11 for each registered trade name, together with the name and address of the agent, if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and renewal (trade names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration of a trade name is valid for 10 years from date of filing; right may be preserved indefinitely through successive renewals every 10 years on application in the final year and payment of renewal fee fixed by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner enjoys six-month grace period from expiry to make valid payment with surcharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of trade name — timing and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where protection has not been renewed due to circumstances beyond owner's control, owner or entitled persons may apply for restoration within six months of date circumstances ceased and no later than two years after renewal was due, on payment of renewal fee and surcharge and statement of grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restoration does not extend maximum duration of protection; restored trade names published; rejection appealable within 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renunciation of registered trade name
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner may renounce the trade name at any time by written declaration to the Organization; renunciation takes effect on the date it is entered in the special register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invalidity of trade names — grounds and proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent domestic courts shall declare invalidation of registration on application by public prosecutor or any interested party if inconsistent with Articles 1, 2 and 5(1) or conflicts with a prior right (in which case invalidity may only be declared on application by owner of prior right).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When decision becomes final it shall be notified to Organization for entry in special register; invalidity shall be published per implementing regulations and registration deemed invalid as of date it occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of trade names — requirement to transfer with establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: A trade name may be assigned or transferred only with the trade, industrial, craft or agricultural establishment, or with the part of such establishment designated under the trade name.
